task: Which UK organisations help Chinese and Asian technology companies enter and expand in the UK market (UK soft landing, market entry, representation, landing programmes for science parks and innovation zones)? List the main competitors and alternatives with website URLs, what they offer, and how they position themselves. Include private firms, membership bodies like China-Britain Business Council, accelerators, and government programmes.

result.json_content:
{"result":"The passages provide evidence for a small set of relevant options, mostly China-focused; they do not establish a comprehensive list of UK soft-landing providers for Chinese or Asian tech companies.

| Organisation / route | Website URL in the passages | What it offers | How it fits / positions itself |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strategi Global Solutions (private firm) | https://strategiglobal.co.uk/ | Bespoke, end-to-end UK entry support: company formation and legal-structure guidance; HR, recruitment, payroll and tax setup; regulatory compliance; market-entry and route-to-market strategy; introductions to UK clients, partners and investors; and access to workspace or infrastructure. | The clearest private-sector soft-landing alternative in the passages. It describes its support as hands-on and tailored to a company’s sector, size and growth aims. The passage describes international businesses generally, not a China- or Asia-specific offer. |
| China-Britain Business Council (CBBC; membership body) | https://www.cbbc.org/ | Practical advice and consultancy, market research, events, trade missions and exhibitions, and incorporation support. It also describes membership opportunities, access, seminars and networking; the passages mention hosting Chinese inward delegations and UK/China business events. | The main China-specific membership and business-network option evidenced here. Its stated core mission is helping UK members grow trade and investment with China, so it is a complementary network and market-access route—not clearly a dedicated UK landing service for Chinese entrants. |
| Department for Business and Trade / Invest in UK (government) | https://www.business.gov.uk/invest-in-uk/sectors/technology/ | Government information on UK technology opportunities, regions and sector strengths, with a route to tailor-made help and support for setting up in the UK. A separate passage says DBT in China supports UK businesses accessing China and assists Chinese investors. | Government-facing investment and information route rather than a named, China-specific landing programme. The supplied material does not specify the precise service or application route for Chinese technology companies. |
| UK-China Business & Innovation Hub | No usable website URL is given in the passages. | A hub announced for Suzhou, described as supporting UK and Chinese companies with market-entry and soft-landing support and flexible office space. | A cross-border alternative, but the announced hub is in Suzhou, not the UK; the passage does not establish it as a UK-based landing provider for Chinese firms entering the UK. |
| UK sector accelerators and innovation programmes (adjacent alternatives) | URLs are not supplied in the passages. | The government technology-sector page names Cyber Runway, Greater Manchester Digital Security Hub (DiSH) and the Defence and Security Accelerator (DASA) as growth-support examples, and mentions National Quantum Computing Centre SparQ and Digital Catapult access initiatives. | These are described as sector or innovation support, not as China-specific market-entry or UK soft-landing programmes. They may be relevant after a company identifies a UK sector pathway, but the passages do not show that they provide representation, incorporation or general landing services. |

Bottom line: Strategi Global is the strongest evidenced private soft-landing option; CBBC is the strongest evidenced China-focused network and membership body; and the government Invest in UK route is the broad public-sector starting point. The passages do not provide enough support to name additional direct competitors, confirm UK-based science-park landing programmes for Chinese entrants, or give URLs for the Hub and named accelerators. The evidence is China-centred and does not substantiate a broader Asia-specific provider landscape."}
